observations: Photo 0: Black UPS unit with 'BLUE GATE' branding embossed on top front, blue vertical strip with power button and three indicator LEDs, standing on tiled floor.
Photo 1: Same unit from a side/top angle showing power cable with UK-style 3-pin plug, unit resting on its side, no model number, capacity (VA/W) rating, or label visible.
No rating label, serial sticker, or specification plate is visible in either photo.
Unit shows some surface wear/scuffing on casing but no visible cracks or damage.
Unit is not shown powered on or under load in any photo.
Seller's new message is text only, no new photo or video provided.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 and photo 1 show a physical UPS unit

claims.claim: Battery is new, holds charge for 8 hours
claims.evidence: No photo or clip shows the unit running on battery, a timer, or battery receipt/invoice; seller's verbal reassurance is not visual proof
No photo of internal casing/screws or service history provided; seller's word alone does not settle this

claims.claim: I tested it myself yesterday, everything I said is true
claims.evidence: No video, timer, or dated proof of the test was sent; a seller's assurance is not evidence

risks.risk: Battery runtime could be far less than claimed 8 hours, or battery could be old/dead
risks.proof: Video clip of unit running a load (e.g., lamp or fan) on battery power with a visible timer, or a dated receipt for battery replacement
risks.if_unproven: priced as battery not holding charge / needing replacement

risks.risk: No VA/Watt capacity rating visible, so unclear what loads it can support
risks.proof: Clear photo of the rating label/sticker (usually on the back or bottom) showing VA/W output
risks.if_unproven: priced at the low end of typical capacity for this form factor

risks.risk: Unit could have hidden internal repairs or non-original parts despite 'never repaired' claim
risks.proof: Photo of opened casing showing untouched seals/screws, or original purchase receipt

risks.risk: Unit not demonstrated powering on or functioning at all
risks.proof: Video clip of unit being switched on with LEDs lighting and audible beep/fan
risks.if_unproven: priced as non-functional until shown working

proof_requests: Video clip of the UPS running a load on battery power with a visible clock/timer to support the 8-hour claim
Clear photo of the rating/specification label (VA/W output) usually on the back or base
Video of the unit powering on from mains showing LED indicators and any audible signals
Photo of the battery itself or compartment if accessible, and any purchase receipt for 'new' battery claim
response.reason: A verbal reassurance with no new photo or video does not change the evidence; the rating label needed even for a worst-case price is still missing, and the runtime and repair claims remain unverifiable from photos alone.
